title: Spinach and cheese breakfast casserole

items: 1 Tbsp butter, plus 1 tsp for the dish
½ medium yellow onion, finely diced
2 cups packed fresh baby spinach, roughly chopped
2 cups frozen shredded hash browns, thawed

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle. Butter a 9×9-inch baking dish.
Melt 1 Tbsp butter in a 10-inch skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 4–5 min, until soft and translucent. Add the spinach and stir 1–2 min, just until wilted. Let it cool a few minutes.
Pat the thawed hash browns dry with paper towels and spread them in the dish. Scatter the onion and spinach on top.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper until smooth. Pour it over the vegetables and sprinkle the cheese evenly on top.
Bake 45–55 min, until puffed and golden, the center no longer jiggles when you nudge the dish, and a thermometer in the center reads 160°F.
Rest 10 min so it sets, then cut into 6 pieces.
tips: Using frozen chopped spinach? Thaw 5 oz, squeeze it very dry in a towel and skip the wilting.
Assemble it the night before, cover and refrigerate. Bake straight from the fridge and add 10–15 min.
In an 8×8-inch dish it sits deeper, so start checking at 55 min.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days, covered. Reheat a piece in the microwave 60–90 sec, until hot in the center. Freeze single pieces, wrapped, up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating.
